United StatesPDF page 7 · Data Collection

Field dates and setting

Online survey; overall multinational window July 2020–January 2024; United States-specific dates NR.
using three survey firmsPDF page 7 · Data Collection

Fieldwork ran July 2020–January 2024 through IPSOS, Netquest, and PureSpectrum, with the country-to-firm mapping reported.

Number recruited and analyzed

Country-specific recruited/randomized/analyzed totals NR. Pooled: >17,000 surveyed and 13,274 analyzed. Figure 4 reports n=443 for the focal sexual-harassment country display.
final sample consisted of 13,274 respondentsPDF page 7 · Data Collection

More than 17,000 were surveyed; manipulation-check failures and very fast completers were removed, leaving 13,274. Exact recruited and randomized counts are absent.

n = 443 for the US, and n = 632 for the UKPDF page 12 · Figure 4 note

Figure 4 supplies country-specific sexual-harassment sample sizes and plots all three arm means for the United States and United Kingdom, with unlabeled error bars.

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Three council-composition arms crossed with two issue areas (six cells).
varies on two dimensionsPDF page 5 · Experimental Design and Measurement

Unit of randomization

Respondent (determinate from respondent-level exposure to one vignette; not stated in a standalone randomization sentence).
survey experiment in which respondents across 12 countriesPDF page 5 · Experimental Design and Measurement

three questions immediately following the vignettePDF page 6 · Experimental Design and Measurement

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

NR; stratification and assignment restrictions are also NR.

Exact treatment and comparator

All-male council; four-men/four-women council with no election-path information; four-men/four-women council elected under an equal-candidate rule. Issue is sexual-harassment training or animal-mistreatment training. Full vignette wording NR in the main article.

Target population

Nationally representative online population with internet access in Norway.

Proprietary-panel respondents with internet access were selected on demographic dimensions; this states the target and panel recruitment approach.

Eligibility criteria

Internet access; additional panel eligibility criteria NR.
nationally representative sample of the online populationPDF page 7 · Data Collection

Proprietary-panel respondents with internet access were selected on demographic dimensions; this states the target and panel recruitment approach.

Recruitment procedure

Respondents drawn from IPSOS's proprietary panel; demographic selection used age, race/ethnicity, gender, geography, and country-specific variables.
nationally representative sample of the online populationPDF page 7 · Data Collection

Proprietary-panel respondents with internet access were selected on demographic dimensions; this states the target and panel recruitment approach.

NorwayPDF page 7 · Data Collection

Page 7 identifies IPSOS as the panel provider for Norway; it gives only the overall July 2020–January 2024 field window, not country-specific dates.

Field dates and setting

Online survey; overall multinational window July 2020–January 2024; Norway-specific dates NR.
using three survey firmsPDF page 7 · Data Collection

Fieldwork ran July 2020–January 2024 through IPSOS, Netquest, and PureSpectrum, with the country-to-firm mapping reported.

Number recruited and analyzed

Country-specific recruited/randomized/analyzed totals NR. Pooled: >17,000 surveyed and 13,274 analyzed.
final sample consisted of 13,274 respondentsPDF page 7 · Data Collection

More than 17,000 were surveyed; manipulation-check failures and very fast completers were removed, leaving 13,274. Exact recruited and randomized counts are absent.

Experimental arms or randomized attributes

Three council-composition arms; sexual-harassment issue only.
varies on two dimensionsPDF page 5 · Experimental Design and Measurement

Council composition has three levels; issue area has sexual-harassment and animal-mistreatment levels. The page gives the randomized council-composition sentence, but the full six vignettes are only pointed to in excluded supplementary material.

exclude France, Norway, and AustraliaPDF page 11 · footnote 19

Footnote 19 states these three later country samples included only the women's-rights issue, so they are three-arm survey experiments rather than 3×2 factorials.

Unit of randomization

Respondent (determinate from respondent-level exposure to one vignette; not stated in a standalone randomization sentence).
survey experiment in which respondents across 12 countriesPDF page 5 · Experimental Design and Measurement

The design exposes respondents to a fictional city-council newspaper story in 12 countries.

three questions immediately following the vignettePDF page 6 · Experimental Design and Measurement

The article prints three substantive-legitimacy items and three procedural-legitimacy items and identifies the reversal of the overturned item.

Allocation probabilities and restrictions

NR; stratification and assignment restrictions are also NR.

Exact treatment and comparator

All-male council; four-men/four-women council with no election-path information; four-men/four-women council elected under an equal-candidate rule. Issue is sexual-harassment training. Full vignette wording NR in the main article.
varies on two dimensionsPDF page 5 · Experimental Design and Measurement

Council composition has three levels; issue area has sexual-harassment and animal-mistreatment levels. The page gives the randomized council-composition sentence, but the full six vignettes are only pointed to in excluded supplementary material.

complete wording for all six treatment conditionsPDF page 6 · Experimental Design and Measurement

The main article says full condition wording is in Supplementary Material SI.D; that pointer does not supply the omitted text.

Outcome definitions and timing

Immediately post-vignette substantive- and procedural-legitimacy composites, each based on three printed questions (procedural scale has one item in France, Australia, and Norway); 1–4 responses, one reverse-coded item, within-country standardization.
three questions immediately following the vignettePDF page 6 · Experimental Design and Measurement

The article prints three substantive-legitimacy items and three procedural-legitimacy items and identifies the reversal of the overturned item.

standardize responses within countriesPDF page 6 · Experimental Design and Measurement

Composite legitimacy scores retain the approximate 1–4 scale and are standardized to country-standard-deviation units, but the exact item-combination operation is not stated.

Estimand

Mean arm contrasts in standardized legitimacy, including each gender-balanced arm versus all-male and the quota penalty (quota-elected minus non-quota gender-balanced).
difference in respondents’ average legitimacy beliefsPDF page 10 · Quota Penalties Moderated by Quota Threshold

The quota penalty is explicitly the mean legitimacy difference between the gender-balanced and quota-elected gender-balanced arms; other effects compare each with all-male councils.

Estimator or statistical model

Arm averages and differences in arm-average standardized scores; exact composite formula and uncertainty model NR.
